info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package risk is Hanzo Risk: the scoring and decision plane for any entity a tenant has — an account, a transaction, a session, an agent, a merchant, a payout — and the shared model plane both it and the compliance face read.

post.summary: Fit a calibration so a score reads as a probability
post.description:
Calibrate fits the map that turns this organisation's scores into
probabilities, from its own judged decisions.

A detector's score is a density — how isolated an event is among the mass this
organisation's recent traffic laid down. It ranks well and it means nothing on
its own: 0.8 is not "80% likely", and two organisations' 0.8s are not
comparable. Every band set on such a score is a number someone liked and every
cost calculation over it is arithmetic on the wrong units.

The fit is refused rather than approximated when the evidence cannot support
one — too few judged decisions, or all of them one class — because a
calibration fitted on one class is a constant, and a constant reported as a
probability is a lie with a decimal point on it.

It records the SCORING SHAPE it was fitted under: the detector's geometry and
feature inventory folded with this organisation's enabled rule set. If either
moves, the map refuses to answer and the decision plane reports probabilities
as absent — which is the training-serving skew control, and the reason it
cannot fail silently.

get.summary: Read the calibration in force and how well it holds
get.description:
Calibration reads the map in force and how well it holds against reality.

The reliability report is the diagonal a console draws: bins of predicted
probability against the share that actually turned out productive. An empty
bin reports absence rather than zero, because a point drawn at zero on that
chart claims perfect confidence in innocence.

Current is the field to read first. When it is false the scoring shape has
moved since the fit — a feature changed, or a rule was written, retired or
reweighted — and the map refuses to answer, so every decision since reports
its probability as absent. The remedy is a new fit, and until then the bands
cannot act.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description:
Stage selects whose bands supply the operating point and the prices.
Empty measures at the cost-minimising threshold with no stated price,
which reports separation and nothing about money.

parameters.name: horizon
parameters.description:
Horizon is the maturity horizon in days, 0 to 3650 — see mlCalibrate, where
the same field decides the same thing and for the same reason.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Rows bounds the history read, 1..50000. Zero takes the bound.

post.summary: Measure the decision plane against what actually happened
post.description:
Evaluate measures the decision plane against what actually happened.

The metrics suit imbalanced data because fraud is rare and the usual ones do
not: accuracy is not computed at all, ROC-AUC is reported with the prevalence
beside it because it is uninterpretable without one, and average precision is
computed by the step definition rather than the trapezoid — interpolating
between operating points on a precision-recall curve credits a plane with
points it cannot reach, and flatters exactly the rare-event case the metric
exists for.

The cost-weighted number is the one anybody outside the team cares about. A
miss and a false alarm have different prices, both stated on the stage's own
bands, both integers of nano-units so the arithmetic is exact. The
cost-minimising threshold is reported beside the one in force, and the gap
between them is what a threshold review is about.

Unacted bounds the trust in all of it: a blocked decision has no outcome, so a
judged set drawn only from decisions the plane already acted on measures
agreement with the incumbent rather than accuracy.

get.summary: Read the typology-to-feature inventory the model is built on
get.description:
Features is the typology-to-feature inventory the model is built on: what each
dimension measures, the risk indicator it serves, and the published source
those words come from.

It is code rather than a document because a mapping kept beside the model
cannot drift away from what the model actually reads — and the attributability
it makes possible is why this is a tree and not a net.

get.summary: Read the learning curve: quality against how much history was seen
get.description:
Learning is the curve an operator reads before spending money on more labels:
quality as a function of how much history the fit had.

It has TWO arms and the pair is the point. The train arm is the metric on the
rows the fit saw, optimistic by construction. The ahead arm is the metric on a
FIXED later window — the same rows at every step, all of them after everything
any step trained on. Both still falling means more labels would help; the
train arm falling while the ahead arm has stopped means the fit has started
memorising the sample and the next thing to change is the method, not the
volume.

The split is temporal and only temporal, never random. A random split lets a
fit see the future — fraud arrives in campaigns, and half a campaign on each
side of the line scores brilliantly on a pattern the fit has already been
shown — and lets one device or one card appear on both sides, which rewards
memorising an identifier and is invisible in every metric.

The separation arm and the calibration arm say different things: a monotone
calibration cannot reorder anything, so ROC and PR are identical before and
after fitting one. ROC and PR moving along the curve is the DETECTOR getting
better as it learns; Brier moving is the CALIBRATION getting better as labels
accrue.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: Method is isotonic or platt, as for a fit.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description: Stage supplies the prices, so the cost arm of the curve means something.

parameters.name: horizon
parameters.description: Horizon is the maturity horizon in days, 0 to 3650.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.description: Steps is how many points the curve has, 2..20, default 10.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Rows bounds the history read, 1..50000. Zero takes the bound.

post.summary: Replay a candidate policy over this tenant's own history
post.description:
Replay answers what a candidate policy WOULD have decided, over the decisions
this organisation already made.

The RECORDED score is replayed and the model is not re-run, for two reasons
that are the difference between a backtest that means something and one that
does not. A score states how unusual an event was against the traffic at that
moment, so recomputing it against today's aggregates answers a different
question under the same name. And the detector has since learned from these
very events, so re-scoring them through it is the purest form of knowing the
future — and it produces a beautiful number.

So the score is a fact and the candidate is a pure function of it, which is
what makes the report DETERMINISTIC: no clock, no random source, no model
state, and nothing that reaches the output is a map. Two runs over the same
rows return the same digest, which is what lets a replay be evidence.

It is written down. A replay is the justification attached to a threshold
change, so it is a record with an identifier and not a number that scrolled
past in a console.

get.summary: Read a replay report
get.description:
Reads a replay back. A threshold change is justified by one, so
the justification has to still be there when somebody asks about the change.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the record to read, from the path.

post.summary: Restore this tenant's learned state from its pinned snapshot
post.description:
Restore reinstates this tenant's learned state from its pinned snapshot.

A snapshot whose shape does not match the running inventory is REFUSED, not
coerced, and a snapshot belonging to another tenant is refused twice — here,
by the tenant that asked, and again inside the engine. State the model would
treat as its own memory has to have come from this algorithm over this feature
set for this tenant.

post.summary: Score an observation without learning from it
post.description:
Score scores one observation and LEARNS NOTHING from it. It is how a candidate
is tried against a tenant's real behaviour before anything depends on the
answer, and it is the model's analogue of testing a rule: because it records
nothing, the aggregates it reads do not include the candidate.

post.summary: Exhaustively search the model topology over this tenant's own history
post.description:
Search exhaustively tries the model topology over this tenant's own history
and returns the learning curve and the winning shape.

The grid is CLOSED — trees x depth x window x blend x appetite — because an
unbounded grid is an unbounded amount of a shared pod's CPU reachable by
anyone with a key. Each candidate runs in a sandbox over fresh counters, so a
search can never move the live model, and no candidate can see another
tenant's history because the replay reads this tenant's own file.

It answers 202 with a run identifier; read the report back at
GET /v1/ml/search/{id}.

get.summary: Read an exhaustive search's report
get.description:
Reads an exhaustive search's report: every candidate tried, the
winner, and the winner's learning curve.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the record to read, from the path.

post.description:
Snapshot pins this tenant's learned state into its own encrypted file.

It is what an auditor asks for: the exact model that raised an alert, kept so
that the same input can be scored again a year later. It is also what makes a
rollout survivable — the shutdown path snapshots every resident tenant,
because cloud deploys Recreate at one replica and a model that comes back with
nothing learned refuses to score for its whole warm period.

get.summary: Read the model's governance state
get.description:
ModelState is what a review of the model reads: the appetite it was given, the
threshold that appetite produced, and the share it ACTUALLY reached.

Stated against realised is the whole governance report. An appetite is a
measured commitment or it is nothing, and a fixed threshold on a drifting
distribution silently becomes either silence or a flood.

put.summary: Set the share of the stream the model may examine
put.description:
Sets how much of the stream the model may examine.

Review is the lever, and the threshold is derived from it as a quantile of the
scores actually observed rather than fixed at a number someone liked. That is
what makes an alert level governed rather than tuned, and it is why the level
cannot be set to fit the size of the review team.

post.summary: Train this tenant's model on its own observations
post.description:
Train teaches this tenant's model from this tenant's own observations.

It is online: there is no job, no queue and no window in which the tenant is
protected by a stale model, because the half-space geometry is built before
any data arrives and the model IS a set of mass counters. One observation is
one increment.

THERE IS NO CROSS-TENANT TRAINING INPUT AND NO WAY TO EXPRESS ONE. The model
is indexed by the tenant key and its tree GEOMETRY is seeded from it, so two
tenants do not merely hold different counters — they hold different trees.
Any cross-org learning in this product is aggregate-only, lives in a table
with no tenant column, and is published only above a k-anonymity floor.

get.summary: Watch live rule activations and their disposition
get.description:
Activity is the watcher: what is firing right now, what is being muted, and
which way the decisions are going.

It reads the DECISION LOG rather than a second bus. The log is already the
record and the analytics copies already reach the platform stream; a dedicated
activation bus would be a third representation of one fact and a third thing
that can be behind.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit bounds how many recent decisions are summarised, 1..500.

get.summary: List the platform controls declared on subjects
get.description:
Controls lists the platform controls declared on this tenant's subjects:
reserves, payout holds and blocks.

They are DECLARATIONS the money plane reads. Risk never moves money —
hanzoai/commerce owns payouts, disputes and balances — so a marketplace reads
this before a payout and calls decide at authorization, and risk touches no
processor. That is what "processor-agnostic" is: a structural property, not a
feature.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Kind narrows to one subject kind.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Subject narrows to one subject.

post.summary: Declare a reserve, a payout hold or a block on a subject
post.description: Declares a reserve, a payout hold or a block on a subject.

delete.description:
Lifts a control. Answers 204, or 404 for an identifier this
tenant does not own.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the record to act on, taken from the path.

post.summary: Score an entity or event and return a decision
post.description:
Decide scores one entity or event and answers what to do about it: allow,
challenge, review, restrict or block, with the evidence behind it.

One op, not three. "Score this thing" is one verb, and a stage-specific op per
lifecycle moment would be three places for the tenant gate to drift. The stage
selects the feature window and the rule set and nothing else.

It is METERED AFTER the work, never gated before it. A pre-work balance gate
would have to render its refusal in the fleet's nested error contract, which a
typed op cannot do — so the hot path stays typed, the screen is billed on the
decision that was actually produced, and no funded client's 402 parsing is
affected. Overage lands on the caller's OWN ledger: Meter sends the org as
both the commerce identity and the org header, which is the anti-cross-org
property.

get.summary: List recent decisions
get.description:
Decisions lists this tenant's recent decisions, newest first. Every filter is
an equality on a column the tenant's own file owns, so a filter can narrow the
caller's own log and can never widen it.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Kind narrows to one subject kind.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Subject narrows to one subject.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Action narrows to one outcome.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description: Stage narrows to one lifecycle moment.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit bounds the page, 1..500, default 100.

get.summary: Read one decision with its evidence
get.description:
Reads one decision with everything behind it: the evidence, the
model's per-feature attribution and the digest of the model that produced it.
That set IS the dispute packet — what was decided, on what, by which model.

A decision another tenant owns answers 404, exactly as an unknown identifier
does, because the tenant's file is the only place looked in: there is no query
that could reach another tenant's row, so a probe learns nothing.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the record to act on, taken from the path.

post.summary: Record what a human concluded about a decision
post.description:
Label records what a human concluded about a decision — fraud, legitimate,
chargeback, abuse or unknown.

THE DECIDER IS SERVER-SET. It comes from the validated principal and never
from the request body: the engine's own resolutions carry an unauthenticated
`by`, and importing that gap into a product that bills on the decision would
make the attribution worthless the moment anyone asked who cleared what.

This is also the only supervision this product has. Everything the model knows
about its own miss rate comes from these labels against the below-the-line
sample.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the decision, from the path.

get.summary: Read the field catalogue a rule may name
get.description:
Dictionary is the vocabulary a rule may be written in: every fact, every
operator, every velocity axis and window, this tenant's own lists, and the
signal keys this tenant has actually sent.

Two lenses on one catalogue. The product half is closed and is what admission
checks against. The tenant half — the signals — is the tenant's own, read back
off its recent decisions, which is what makes a rule builder able to offer the
fields that exist here rather than the fields that exist in general.

get.summary: Report whether the decision plane can decide
get.description:
Answers 200 with a report of what is up, or 503 CARRYING THE SAME REPORT as its body — which is the whole point of a real probe, and the reason this one route is not a typed op: a typed op reaches a non-2xx only by returning an error, and that renders as an envelope with the report dropped.

The report names the model digest in force, how many tenants this process holds resident, whether the feature warehouse is reachable, and whether metering is configured. Only the first is load-bearing for a decision: the rings are in memory, the rules and lists are the tenant's own file, and the model is in process, so a decision does NOT need the warehouse and the probe stays green without it. A warehouse that is down costs the field dictionary and the search sandbox, and is reported as exactly that rather than as a failure of the authorization path.

get.summary: List this tenant's allow and deny lists
get.description:
Lists shows this tenant's allow and deny lists and how many values each holds.

These are the TENANT's operational lists. Sanctions and PEP designations are
not here and are never merged into them: a tenant may add to its own deny
list, and a tenant may not edit OFAC.

post.summary: Create an allow or deny list
post.description: Creates an allow or deny list a rule can name in an inlist term.

Adds values to a list. Values are folded to lower case so a
value added in one case matches a signal sent in another.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the list, from the path.

delete.summary: Remove one value from a list
delete.description:
Removes one value from a list. Answers 204, or 404 when the
list does not hold it.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the list, from the path.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Value is the value to remove, from the path.

get.summary: Read whether this tenant's decisions act or only observe
get.description: Mode reports whether this tenant's decisions act or only observe.

put.summary: Take this tenant live, or return it to shadow
put.description:
Takes this tenant live, or returns it to shadow.

SHADOW IS THE DEFAULT AND THE DEFAULT IS NOT CONFIGURABLE. In shadow every
rule runs, the model scores and learns, every decision is recorded, and the
action is always allow — so what would have happened is readable over real
traffic before anyone depends on it. A model that quietly went live and
started declining payments is the worst failure available here.

get.summary: Read the score bands in force
get.description:
Policy reads the score bands in force, per lifecycle stage.

A band maps a calibrated PROBABILITY to an action, which is why it is a
governed value and not a constant: where the line sits between letting a
customer through and stopping them is a business decision with a price on
either side, and it belongs to the organisation making it. A threshold
compiled into the scoring path is a decision nobody signed and cannot be shown
to have been in force on the day a particular customer was declined.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description:
Stage is signup, payment, session, usage or payout. Empty reads every
stage this organisation has set bands for.

put.summary: Set the score bands, as a new recorded version
put.description:
Records a new version of one stage's bands.

It is an INSERT and never an update. A policy change is a governance decision,
so the previous version stays exactly as it was and "what was in force when
this customer was declined" is a lookup rather than a reconstruction. The
version is minted here, the author comes from the validated principal rather
than from the body, and the reason is required — a threshold that moved with
no stated reason is a decision with no author.

Every refusal below is a real way a ladder silently stops being a risk policy:
a band above one is an action nothing can reach, bands out of order mean a
higher probability asks for less, two bands at one probability leave which
applies undecided, and a band repeating the action beneath it is dead weight
that makes the ladder look like it has more steps than it has.

get.summary: Read every version of a stage's bands, newest first
get.description:
PolicyVersions is the audit trail: every version of one stage's bands, newest
first, each with who set it, when and why.

Nothing here was ever edited, so this is the whole history and not a
reconstruction of one.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description:
Stage is the lifecycle moment. Required: a version history across stages
would interleave unrelated decisions.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit bounds the page, 1..200, default 50.

get.summary: Read the closed vocabulary of reason codes a decision can cite
get.description:
Reasons is the closed vocabulary of reason codes a decision can cite.

It is DERIVED from the detector's own feature inventory rather than declared
beside it, so it cannot name a feature the model does not read and cannot omit
one it does. Every model code carries the typology, the supervisory indicator
and the published citation those words come from, so a reason shown to a
person is checkable rather than asserted.

A free-text reason cannot be counted, cannot be tested and cannot be compared
between two decisions. Every regime that lets someone question an automated
decision asks for the principal reasons specifically — which is a ranked list
over a fixed vocabulary, and this is the vocabulary.

get.summary: List this tenant's rules
get.description:
Rules lists this tenant's detections. A tenant starts with a starter set
covering the lifecycle the product names — signup burst, shared device,
disposable email, card testing, denied address, spend spike, payout velocity,
undeclared automation — all of which it may read, copy, edit and retire.

post.description:
Admits a new detection. Admission is strict on purpose: a rule with
no terms holds on everything, a rule naming a field that does not exist holds
on nothing, and both read as a working control from the outside.

delete.description:
Retires a detection. Answers 204, or 404 for an identifier this
tenant does not own.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the record to act on, taken from the path.

patch.description:
Replaces a detection whole. There is no partial update: a rule is a
conjunction of terms, and merging a partial term list into an existing one is
a change nobody can read off the request.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID is the rule to replace, from the path on a PATCH. Ignored on create,
where the server mints one.

post.summary: Replay a candidate rule over this tenant's own history
post.description:
Simulate replays a candidate rule over this tenant's OWN recorded decisions
and reports what it would have caught, what it would have given up, and how
much of that a human has already judged.

It is a gate and not a nicety: a new typology has to be tested before live
activation, and a retirement has to be justified against the outgoing rule's
performance. Nothing is written — the replay reads the decision log and
evaluates in memory.

An EMPTY history is REFUSED rather than reported as zero alerts. "No alerts"
is exactly what a quiet rule looks like, and being unable to tell the two
apart is the failure a sandbox exists to prevent.

get.summary: Read one subject's current risk state
get.description:
Reads one subject's current risk state: every live velocity
aggregate it has, its recent decisions, whatever controls are declared on it,
its thirty-day history, and where this KIND of subject sits across the
platform. This is the continuous-monitoring read — a merchant, an account or
an agent, on one page.

The last two come from the warehouse and are BEST EFFORT: an unreachable
warehouse omits them and names the gap, because a zeroed history would say the
subject did nothing and a zeroed baseline would say the platform did.

The network comparison is the only cross-org value this API returns and it is
aggregate BY CONSTRUCTION: the table has no tenant column, so there is no
query — here or anywhere — that could return another tenant's rows.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Kind is the subject kind, from the path.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the subject identifier, from the path.

get.summary: List active suppressions
get.description:
Suppressions lists the active mutes. A suppression that has expired is not
listed and mutes nothing — a forgotten mute stops muting instead of quietly
staying on forever.

post.description:
Suppress mutes a rule's activations for a subject, a subject kind, or
everywhere that rule fires.

A suppressed hit is RECORDED with suppressed set and contributes nothing to
the action. It is never dropped, for the same reason the model counts its
refusals: silence must never read as a clean result, and a compliance record
that can be silently muted by an operational knob is not a record.

delete.description:
Unsuppress lifts a mute. Answers 204, or 404 for an identifier this tenant
does not own.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the record to act on, taken from the path.

review.description:
Review is the share of the stream that may be sent for examination. The
alert threshold is derived from it as a quantile of the scores actually
observed, rather than fixed at a number someone liked — so an alert level
is governed rather than tuned, and a drifting distribution does not turn
it into silence or a flood.

sample.description:
Sample is the share of NON-alerting traffic retained for review below the
line. It is the only instrument that can measure what the model missed,
because nothing in the stream is labelled.

warm.description: Warm is how many observations the model must learn before it may score.

review.description: Review is the share of the stream that may be examined, in (0, 0.5].

sample.description: Sample is the share of non-alerting traffic retained, in [0, 1].

from.description: From is the lower bound of the predicted probability, inclusive.

observed.description:
Observed is the share of them that turned out productive. A calibrated map
has it equal to Predicted, and the gap between the two is the whole report.
Absent for an empty bin, for the same reason.

predicted.description:
Predicted is the mean probability the map gave them. ABSENT for an empty
bin: a point drawn at zero would claim perfect confidence in innocence.

rows.description: Rows is how many decisions fell in the bin.

to.description: To is the upper bound, exclusive.

horizon.description:
Horizon is how many days a decision must have aged before its outcome
counts as settled. It is the single most consequential field here: an
analyst judges within hours and a card dispute lands 30 to 120 days later,
so measuring over everything strips the recent tail of exactly the
chargebacks that make the base rate what it is. 120 for a payment lane, 14
for signup abuse, 0 only where every label genuinely arrives at once.
Between 0 and 3650, which is past every retention window here.

method.description:
Method is isotonic or platt. Isotonic assumes only that a higher score is
never less likely to be productive, which is the one assumption the
detector guarantees, and needs data. Platt has two parameters and survives
a small sample at the cost of assuming a shape. Empty takes isotonic.

rows.description: Rows bounds the history read, 1..50000. Zero takes the bound.

at.description: At is when it was fitted, RFC 3339 in UTC.

brier.description:
Brier is the mean squared error on the fitting sample — the in-sample
number, and therefore optimistic. The honest one is on the learning
curve's held-out arm.

current.description:
Current says whether that shape is still the one in force. When it is not,
the map REFUSES to answer and every decision reports its probability as
absent — which is the training-serving skew control working, and the field
to read first.

digest.description:
Digest identifies this fit exactly, so a decision can name the map that
produced its probability.

fitted.description:
Fitted is false when this organisation has no calibration. Everything
below is then empty and the decision plane reports probabilities as
absent rather than inventing them.

horizon.description: Horizon is the maturity horizon the fit was taken under, in days.

immature.description:
Immature is how many labelled decisions that horizon excluded for being too
young. A horizon that quietly drops most of the evidence is the difference
between a thin answer and a wrong one, so it is reported beside every fit.

prevalence.description:
Prevalence is the productive share of that sample. A probability read
without it is uninterpretable: 0.4 is alarming at a base rate of one in a
thousand and unremarkable at one in three.

productive.description: Productive is how many of them turned out to be worth acting on.

refusal.description: Refusal names why there is no fit, when there is none.

reliability.description:
Reliability is the fit against reality, in bins — the diagonal a console
draws. ABSENT when the map refuses to answer: a reliability report is the
map applied to every row, so a chart beside a refusal draws what the
refusal just said does not exist.

rows.description: Rows is how many judged decisions the fit was taken over.

shape.description:
Shape is the scoring shape it was fitted under: the detector's geometry and
feature inventory folded with this organisation's enabled rule set.

superseded.description:
Superseded is how many mature judged decisions were excluded because they
were scored under a DIFFERENT scoring shape. A fit reads one coordinate
system only — stamping today's shape on yesterday's scores is exactly the
skew the shape gate refuses — so this is the evidence a refit cannot
honestly use, and the number that says why a fit went thin after a governed
change.

truncated.description:
Truncated says the bounded read cut the history: there are older mature
decisions under this shape that nothing here was computed from. The read
takes the MOST RECENT rows, so what is missing is the oldest.

unproductive.description:
Unproductive is how many turned out fine. Both classes are reported so the
imbalance is visible before anyone reads a probability computed over it.

version.description: Version is monotone; a fit never replaces an earlier one in place.

blend.description: Blend is how much of a closing window folds into the reference.

depth.description: Depth is how deep each tree splits.

review.description: Review is the share of the stream this topology may examine.

trees.description: Trees is how many half-space trees the model holds.

window.description: Window is how many observations make up one reference window.

fn.description:
FN is productive and let through — the misses, which the price of a miss
values.

fp.description:
FP is unproductive and flagged — the false alarms, which the price of an
alarm values.

tn.description: TN is unproductive and let through: correctly left alone.

tp.description: TP is productive and flagged: caught.

citation.description: Citation is where those words come from, so the claim is checkable.

indicator.description: Indicator is the supervisor's own words for what is being looked for.

neutral.description:
Neutral is the value at which this feature is unremarkable — the
coordinate the counterfactual moves it to.

severity.description: Severity is the grading a hit on this feature carries.

typology.description: Typology is the pattern it expresses.

unit.description: Unit is how to read the raw number.

window.description: Window is the span it is measured over, when it has one.

digest.description: Digest is the identity of this shape.

items.description:
Items is every dimension, in coordinate order. The ORDER is part of the
model's identity: adding, removing or reordering one invalidates learned
state, which the digest enforces.

horizon.description: Horizon is the maturity horizon applied, in days.

immature.description: Immature is how many labelled decisions that horizon excluded.

refusal.description: Refusal names why the curve is empty when it is.

steps.description: Steps is the curve, oldest prefix first.

superseded.description:
Superseded is how many mature judged decisions were scored under a
different scoring shape and therefore appear at no step.

truncated.description: Truncated says the bounded read cut the history at its oldest end.

ahead.description:
Ahead is the report on the held window, strictly later than anything the
fit saw. Two arms, because one alone cannot tell "more labels would help"
from "the fit has started memorising".

held.description:
Held is the size of the fixed later window this step was measured against.
It is the same at every step, which is the whole reason two steps are
comparable.

judged.description:
Judged is how many of those carried an outcome — the number that actually
constrains the fit.

productive.description:
Productive is how many of the judged were positive. A step with two
positives produces a number and not evidence, and this is how a reader
tells which.

refusal.description:
Refusal names why a step produced no fit — almost always too little of one
class by that point. Stated rather than skipped, so the curve shows where
the plane became able to answer at all.

rows.description: Rows is how many decisions the fit was given.

train.description:
Train is the report on the rows the fit saw, and is optimistic by
construction.

horizon.description:
Horizon is the maturity horizon in days, 0 to 3650 — see mlCalibrate, where
the same field decides the same thing and for the same reason.

rows.description: Rows bounds the history read, 1..50000. Zero takes the bound.

stage.description:
Stage selects whose bands supply the operating point and the prices.
Empty measures at the cost-minimising threshold with no stated price,
which reports separation and nothing about money.

calibrated.description:
Calibrated says whether a probability was available at all. When it is
false, Brier is absent and the operating point is the raw score — the
SAME state the decide path is in, which is the point: this op must not
describe a world the live plane refuses to enter.

curve.description:
Curve is the sweep — ROC, precision-recall and cost, three charts from one
pass because they are three projections of it.

horizon.description: Horizon is the maturity horizon applied, in days.

immature.description:
Immature is how many labelled decisions that horizon excluded for being too
young for their outcome to have arrived.

metrics.description: Metrics is the report at the operating point.

refusal.description: Refusal names why there was no probability, when there was none.

stage.description:
Stage is whose bands supplied the operating point and the prices, when one
did.

superseded.description:
Superseded is how many mature judged decisions were scored under a
different scoring shape and therefore measured nowhere here.

truncated.description: Truncated says the bounded read cut the history at its oldest end.

unacted.description:
Unacted is the share of the judged evidence that came from decisions the
plane LET THROUGH. It is the honest limit on every number above: a blocked
decision has no outcome, so a judged set made entirely of decisions the
incumbent chose to act on measures agreement with the incumbent rather than
accuracy. Near zero means exactly that.

alarm.description:
Alarm is the share of the judged stream flagged there — the realised
review rate an operations team is resourced against.

best_nano.description:
BestNano is the lowest cost reachable anywhere on the sweep. Absent for the
same reason.

best_threshold.description:
BestThreshold is where that lowest cost sits. The gap between it and
Threshold is what a threshold review is about.

brier.description:
Brier is the calibration error. A well-ranked, badly-calibrated plane
makes every band mean something other than what it says, and neither ROC
nor PR can see that: both are rank statistics and a monotone calibration
cannot move either.

confusion.description: Confusion is the four counts there.

cost_nano.description:
CostNano is what being wrong cost at the operating point, in nano-units of
the organisation's accounting currency. Absent when the stage's bands state
no price, because a cost computed from unstated prices is a number with a
decimal point and no meaning.

f1.description:
F1 is their harmonic mean. It is reported for continuity with what people
expect and it hides the trade-off the two prices make explicit; read the
cost instead when one is stated.

judged.description:
Judged is how many of those carry an outcome. The gap between it and Rows
is the honest limit on everything below, which is why the pair is reported
first.

lift.description:
Lift is precision over prevalence: how much better than chance the flagged
set is. One means the plane is choosing at random.

pr.description:
PR is average precision — the area under precision-recall by the step
definition, never the trapezoid. This is the number that moves when a
rare-event model gets better.

precision.description:
Precision is the productive share of what was flagged at that point — the
number an investigator experiences as the alert queue's hit rate.

prevalence.description: Prevalence is the productive share of the judged set.

productive.description: Productive is how many judged decisions were worth acting on.

recall.description:
Recall is the flagged share of what was productive: how much of the harm
was caught.

refusal.description: Refusal names why a report is thin when it is.

roc.description:
ROC is the area under the receiver-operating curve, ties counted as half a
win. Insensitive to the base rate, which makes it comparable across
organisations and optimistic-looking on a rare-event stream.

rows.description: Rows is every decision looked at.

threshold.description: Threshold is the score everything below is measured at.

unproductive.description:
Unproductive is how many were not. Both classes are reported so the
imbalance is visible before anyone reads a rate computed over it.

alerted.description: Alerted is how many of those it alerted on — the numerator of Realised.

appetite.description: Appetite is the stated share of the stream that may be examined.

blind.description:
Blind counts, per feature, how often it took its neutral value for want of
data.

digest.description: Digest is the model identity an auditor pins.

distribution.description:
Distribution is the score distribution the threshold is cut from, in 32
bands.

inventory.description:
Inventory is the feature set, so the state and the shape are read
together.

learned.description: Learned is how many observations this tenant's model has taken in.

realised.description:
Realised is the share that ACTUALLY alerted. Stated against realised is
the governance report — an appetite is a measured commitment or it is
nothing.

refusals.description:
Refusals counts what the model declined to score, by reason. None of these
was examined by the model; all of them were examined by the rules.

saturated.description:
Saturated means the appetite cannot be honoured by any threshold because
too much of the stream scores in the top band. It is the one state that
must never be mistaken for quiet.

scored.description:
Scored is how many observations the model was able to score — the
denominator of Realised.

threshold.description:
Threshold is the score cut currently in force, recomputed each window as
the quantile that admits the stated share.

warming.description:
Warming is true while the model has not learned enough to score. A warming
model REFUSES rather than scoring low, and the refusal is counted below.

at.description: At is when it was decided, RFC 3339 in UTC.

id.description: ID is the decision this move is about.

outcome.description:
Outcome is what turned out to be true, when anyone judged it. It is what
turns a list of differences into a list of improvements or of regressions.

probability.description:
Probability is what the calibration makes of that score. Absent when no
calibration is in force or the one on file was fitted under another shape.

score.description:
Score is what the model recorded at the time. It is replayed, never
recomputed: the rings have moved on and the detector has since learned from
this very event.

was.description: Was is what the plane actually did.

would.description: Would is what the candidate would have done instead.

amount.description: Amount is the money involved, if any.

at.description: At is when it happened, RFC 3339. Absent means now.

signals.description: Signals are the observations: ip, device, counterparty and the rest.

subject.description: Subject is whose behaviour this is.

cost_nano.description:
CostNano is what this point costs under the stated prices, zero when none
are stated.

fpr.description:
FalsePositive is fall-out: the flagged share of what was unproductive. The
ROC horizontal axis.

precision.description:
Precision is the productive share of what was flagged. The PR vertical
axis, against TruePositive as recall.

threshold.description: Threshold is the score at or above which a decision is flagged.

tpr.description:
TruePositive is recall at this point — the ROC vertical axis, and the PR
horizontal one.

bands.description:
Bands is the candidate ladder. Empty replays the ladder currently in force,
which is how a change of maturity horizon or of window is compared on its
own.

cost.description:
Cost is what being wrong is worth under the candidate. Empty takes the
prices the stage's current bands state.

floor.description:
Floor is the action below the first band. Empty takes the floor the stage's
current ladder states.

horizon.description: Horizon is the maturity horizon in days, 0 to 3650.

rows.description: Rows bounds the history read, 1..50000. Zero takes the bound.

stage.description:
Stage is which lifecycle moment's decisions to replay. Required: replaying
a payout ladder over signup decisions answers a question nobody asked.

at.description: At is when it was run, RFC 3339 in UTC.

calibration.description:
Calibration is the digest of the map that turned each recorded score into
the probability the ladder read. Empty when none was in force.

changed.description: Changed is how many decisions would differ, exactly, and is never cut.

digest.description:
Digest is the identity of this report. Two replays of one candidate over
one history agree on it; if they do not, the inputs moved. It is what makes
a replay evidence rather than an anecdote.

explore.description:
Explore is the share of the judged evidence that came from the
below-the-line sample rather than from something the plane chose to look
at. Near zero means the report is measuring agreement with the incumbent,
which is a property of the evidence and not of the candidate.

from.description: From is the earliest decision in the period, RFC 3339 in UTC.

id.description:
ID identifies this report for the whole of its life. A threshold change is
justified by one, so the justification has an address.

loosened.description:
Loosened is how many it would let through that the plane did not. That
direction is the one a review has to justify.

metrics.description:
Metrics is the candidate measured against the judged subset at the
operating point its FIRST band implies — the point where it stops doing
nothing.

moved.description:
Moved lists the differences, oldest first, cut at a bound. Changed is
never cut.

policy.description: Policy is the digest of the candidate ladder that was replayed.

refusal.description:
Refusal names why a report is empty when it is. An empty history and a
candidate that changes nothing render identically otherwise.

rows.description: Rows is how many decisions were replayed.

tightened.description: Tightened is how many of those the candidate would act harder on.

was.description:
Was is the action distribution the plane actually produced, ascending by
action.

would.description: Would is the distribution the candidate would have produced.

alert.description: Alert is whether this would become evidence.

causes.description: Causes is the per-feature attribution, ordered by contribution.

cut.description: Cut is the threshold in force, derived from the appetite.

model.description: Model is the digest of the model that produced this.

refusal.description: Refusal names the decline: warming or unidentified.

score.description:
Score is the anomaly score in [0,1]: 0 where this tenant's recent
behaviour is densest, 1 where there is none of it.

scored.description: Scored is false when the model declined; Refusal says which refusal.

shadow.description: Shadow is whether the model is observing rather than contributing.

values.description: Values is every coordinate, including the blind ones.

limit.description:
Limit bounds how many recorded observations are replayed, 1..5000. The
grid itself is closed and needs no bound from the caller.

curve.description:
Curve is the winner's separation as a function of how much history it had
seen, in ten steps — the learning curve.

events.description: Events is how many historical observations were replayed.

refusal.description:
Refusal names why the report is empty when it is. An empty history is
refused rather than reported as zero alerts, because a quiet model and an
unrun model produce the same number.

trials.description: Trials is every candidate tried, best-separating first.

winner.description:
Winner is the best-separating topology that also honoured its stated
appetite. Absent when no candidate did both.

candidates.description: Candidates is how many topologies will be tried.

id.description: ID identifies the run; read it back at GET /v1/ml/search/{id}.

at.description: At is when it was pinned, RFC 3339 in UTC.

digest.description: Digest is the model identity that was pinned.

learned.description: Learned is how many observations that state had taken in.

count.description: Count is how many decisions reached it.

observations.description:
Observations are what to learn from. They are this tenant's own data and
nothing else: there is no cross-tenant training input and no way to
express one, because the model is indexed by the tenant key and its tree
GEOMETRY is seeded from it.

learned.description: Learned is how many observations were incorporated.

model.description: Model is the digest of the model that learned them.

refused.description: Refused is how many were not, by reason.

warm.description:
Warm is true once the model has learned enough of this tenant's behaviour
to score at all.

alerted.description: Alerted is how many of those it would have alerted on.

realised.description: Realised is Alerted over Scored, against the Review share intended.

scored.description: Scored is how many observations it was able to score.

separation.description:
Separation is the mean score of the alerted set minus the mean of the
rest. It is the ranking objective: a topology that separates the tail from
the body is doing the job whatever its absolute scores look like.

warm.description: Warm is how many observations passed before it would score at all.

baseline.description: Baseline is what is unremarkable here.

blind.description:
Blind is true when this feature had no usable coordinate, so it took its
neutral value. A feature blind on most traffic is not contributing
whatever the inventory claims for it.

observed.description: Observed is the raw number behind it.

unit.description: Unit is how to read Observed and Baseline.

x.description: X is the coordinate the model used, in [0,1].

activations.description: Activations is how many of the sampled decisions it fired on.

rule.description: Rule is the rule that fired.

suppressed.description: Suppressed is how many of those were muted.

actions.description: Actions is how many decisions reached each action.

agency.description: Agency is how many decisions were of each actor class.

refusals.description: Refusals is how many decisions the model declined to score, by reason.

rules.description: Rules is per-rule activation, most active first.

sampled.description: Sampled is how many recent decisions this summarises.

shadow.description: Shadow is whether this tenant is observing rather than acting.

agent.description:
Agent is the agent reference the caller claims to be acting as. It is
resolved against THIS org's agent registry; an unresolvable reference is
simply not a declaration.

credential.description:
Credential is the credential class the caller believes it presented.
Advisory only — the server reads the credential it actually verified.

session.description: Session is the session reference this action belongs to.

direction.description:
Direction is whether value came in or went out: "in" or "out". Without it
the model cannot see funds passing through, which is the layering shape.

nano.description: Nano is the amount in billionths of one unit of Currency.

action.description: Action is what to do at or above it: challenge, review, restrict or block.

at.description:
At is the boundary, in [0,1]. It is a PROBABILITY and not a raw score —
a band over an uncalibrated score is a band over units that mean nothing,
and the cost arithmetic beneath it would be meaningless too.

day.description: Day is the period the band covers, YYYY-MM-DD.

feature.description: Feature is what is being compared.

observations.description: Observations is how many measurements the band was cut from.

orgs.description:
Orgs is how many distinct organisations contributed to this band. It is
reported so a reader can see the k-anonymity floor was met rather than
take it on trust.

q10.description: Q10 is the tenth percentile across the platform for this subject kind.

q99.description:
Q99 is the ninety-ninth — where the tail this product is looking for
begins.

baseline.description: Baseline is what is unremarkable for this subject.

citation.description: Citation is where those words come from.

indicator.description: Indicator is the supervisor's own words for what is being looked for.

share.description: Share is this feature's part of the score, in [0,1].

typology.description: Typology is the pattern the feature expresses.

unit.description: Unit is how to read Observed and Baseline.

without.description:
Without is the score the model would have produced with this feature
neutral, holding everything else.

at.description: At is when, RFC 3339 in UTC.

by.description: By is who declared it, taken from the validated principal.

rate.description: Rate is the reserve fraction, for a reserve.

reason.description: Reason is why it was declared.

subject.description: Subject is what it applies to.

until.description: Until is when it lapses, RFC 3339. Absent means it does not.

control.description: Control is which one: reserve, payout-hold or block.

rate.description: Rate is the reserve fraction, in [0,1], for a reserve.

subject.description: Subject is what the control applies to.

until.description: Until is when it lapses, RFC 3339. Absent means it does not.

items.description: Items is every control, newest first.

alarm.description:
Alarm is the price of stopping something that was fine: an abandoned
purchase, a support contact, and the share of those customers who do not
come back.

miss.description:
Miss is the price of letting through what should have been stopped — on a
payment lane, typically the disputed amount plus the network's fee.

actor.description: Actor is who is acting, if the caller knows.

amount.description: Amount is the money involved, for the stages where there is any.

idem.description:
Idem makes a re-decide idempotent: the same key returns the same decision
rather than scoring twice and moving the counters twice.

signals.description:
Signals are the observations the caller can supply: ip, email,
emaildomain, device, bin, asn, country, counterparty. Unknown keys are
carried and are readable by a rule as signal.<key>, so a tenant can score
on facts only it has.

subject.description: Subject is what is being judged.

action.description: Action is what to do: allow, challenge, review, restrict or block.

agency.description:
Agency is what kind of actor this was: agent, human, bot or unknown.
Derived server-side from the credential class, this org's agent registry,
the live agent session and the account's metered shape — never from a
user-agent string, which is a claim rather than a fact.

calibration.description: Calibration is the digest of the map that produced Probability.

causes.description: Causes is the model's per-feature attribution, when the model contributed.

hits.description: Hits is the evidence, strongest first.

id.description:
ID identifies this decision for the whole of its life: the label, the
evidence read and the dispute packet all key on it.

model.description:
Model is the digest of the model that produced this, so an auditor can pin
the exact geometry that raised an alert.

policy.description:
Policy is the digest of the score bands that read the probability, so an
auditor can pin exactly which ladder was in force. Empty when no bands are
set for this stage, in which case the evidence alone decided.

probability.description:
Probability is what the score MEANS rather than how it ranks: the
calibrated likelihood in [0,1]. ABSENT — not zero — when this organisation
has no calibration fitted, or when the one it has was fitted under a
scoring shape that has since moved. A density reported as a probability is
a number that lies, and Refusal says which case applies.

reasons.description:
Reasons is the adverse-action artefact: the principal reasons this went the
way it did, strongest first, each a code from the closed vocabulary
/v1/risk/reasons publishes, with the contribution it made and a sentence a
person can be shown. The model's share is its own exact counterfactual —
one coordinate moved to neutral and rescored on the same trees — never a
surrogate fitted afterwards. Four at most: a list of nine is not an
explanation.

refusal.description:
Refusal names why the model declined to score, when it did: warming,
unidentified or shadow. It is present precisely so that silence never
reads as a clean result.

score.description: Score is the weight-of-evidence score in [0,1].

shadow.description:
Shadow is true when this tenant is observing rather than acting. In shadow
Action is always allow and everything else is computed and recorded.

at.description: At is when it was made, RFC 3339 in UTC.

label.description: Label is what a human later concluded, when anyone has.

refusal.description: Refusal names why the model declined, when it did.

shadow.description: Shadow is whether the decision acted.

items.description: Items is the page, newest first.

calibration.description: Calibration is the digest of the map that produced the probability.

model.description: Model is the digest of the model that produced it.

policy.description:
Policy is the digest of the score bands that read the probability, so an
auditor can pin the ladder that was in force.

probability.description:
Probability is the calibrated likelihood this decision was taken at, as
RECORDED — read back, never recomputed, so it is what was true then and not
what the calibration in force today would say. Absent when none was in
force.

reasons.description:
Reasons is the principal reasons, strongest first: the codes, the weights
and the sentences a person is shown.

refusal.description:
Refusal names why there is no probability, when there is none. Silence and
a low probability render the same on a screen and are opposite facts.

actions.description: Actions are the outcomes, weakest first.

lists.description: Lists are this tenant's own lists, which an inlist term may name.

signals.description:
Signals are the signal keys this tenant has actually sent, which is the
half of the catalogue that is the tenant's own rather than the product's.

field.description: Field is how a rule names it.

kind.description: Kind is what sort of value it holds: "string" or "number".

ops.description: Ops are the comparisons that make sense on it.

bucket.description: Bucket is the five-minute period, RFC 3339 in UTC.

values.description:
Values is each counted feature over that period, keyed by the names
GET /v1/risk/dictionary publishes.

action.description: Action is what this evidence alone asked for.

name.description: Name is the detection's human-readable name.

rule.description: Rule is the identifier of the rule or model that produced this evidence.

suppressed.description:
Suppressed marks evidence a suppression muted. It is reported and
contributes nothing — a muted control that left no trace would be
indistinguishable from one that was never running.

weight.description: Weight is how much it contributed, in [0,1].

id.description: ID is the decision, from the path.

verdict.description:
Verdict is what it turned out to be: fraud, legitimate, chargeback, abuse
or unknown. It is the only supervision this product has, and it is what
turns a false-positive rate from a guess into a measurement.

name.description: Name is the list, from the path.

values.description:
Values are the values to add. They are folded to lower case, so a value
added in one case matches a signal in another.

kind.description: Kind is whether membership allows or denies.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when it was created, RFC 3339 in UTC.

entries.description: Entries is how many values it holds.

kind.description: Kind is whether membership allows or denies: "allow" or "deny".

name.description: Name is the list's identifier, which a rule names in an inlist term.

mode.description:
Mode is "shadow" or "live". Shadow is the default and the default is not
configurable: a model that quietly went live and started declining
payments is the worst failure available here, so going live is an act
somebody performs and can be asked about.

since.description: Since is when it was last changed, RFC 3339 in UTC. Empty means never.

at.description: At is when it took effect, RFC 3339 in UTC.

by.description:
By is who decided. A control that changed and cannot say who changed it is
a control nobody owns.

cost.description:
Cost is what this organisation says being wrong is worth. It is what makes
a threshold defensible rather than chosen, and it is what the
cost-weighted metric is computed from.

digest.description:
Digest identifies what this ladder DECIDES — not who wrote it or when — so
a re-save that changed nothing keeps its identity and a moved threshold
does not.

floor.description: Floor is the action below the first band.

reason.description:
Reason is why it changed. Required on a write: a threshold moved without a
stated reason is a decision with no author.

shadow.description:
Shadow observes without acting: every band is computed and recorded and
the action returned is always the floor. It is a second gate in series
with the tenant's live/shadow mode, so one flag flipped by mistake still
cannot make an organisation act.

stage.description:
Stage is the lifecycle moment this governs. One ladder per stage: the
price of a false decline at signup and at payout are different numbers
about different things.

version.description:
Version is monotone within the stage. A change mints the next one and
nothing is edited, so what was in force on a given day is a lookup rather
than a reconstruction.

items.description: Items is one entry per stage, in stage order.

code.description:
Code is from the closed vocabulary. A free-text reason cannot be counted,
cannot be tested and cannot be defended.

says.description:
Says is the sentence an investigator or a declined customer is shown, with
this decision's own numbers in it.

source.description:
Source names the specific rule, when the code does not. Empty for a model
feature, whose code already names it exactly.

weight.description: Weight is this reason's part of the decision, in [0,1].

items.description:
Items is every code, model codes first in the model's own coordinate
order.

model.description:
Model is the digest of the detector shape these codes were derived from.
The vocabulary is a function of the feature inventory, so this pins which
inventory produced it.

citation.description: Citation is where those words come from, so the claim is checkable.

code.description:
Code is the identifier a decision cites and a report counts. It is part of
the published contract: renaming one invalidates every stored decision
that cites it.

indicator.description: Indicator is the supervisor's own words for what is being looked for.

says.description:
Says is the sentence a person is shown, with no numbers in it. A decision
fills its own numbers in.

severity.description: Severity is the grading a reason with this code carries.

source.description:
Source is where a reason with this code comes from — "model" for a feature
the detector reads, "rule" for a rule this organisation wrote.

typology.description: Typology is the pattern the feature expresses.

action.description: Action is what the rule asks for when it holds.

all.description:
All is the conjunction. An empty conjunction is refused: a rule that holds
on everything is not a detection.

enabled.description:
Enabled governs the live path. A disabled rule still replays, because the
question a simulation asks is what happens ON activation.

id.description: ID is the rule's identifier within this tenant.

name.description: Name is what a reviewer reads in an alert.

severity.description: Severity is the reviewer-facing grading: low, medium, high or critical.

stage.description: Stage narrows the rule to one lifecycle moment; empty means every stage.

weight.description: Weight is how much a hit contributes, in [0,1].

id.description:
ID is the rule to replace, from the path on a PATCH. Ignored on create,
where the server mints one.

items.description: Items is every rule, by identifier.

candidate.description:
Candidate is the rule to try. It is evaluated as activated whatever its
enabled flag says: the question is what happens on activation.

incumbent.description:
Incumbent is the rule the candidate would replace, when it replaces one.
Naming it is what turns a report into a justification for a retirement.

limit.description: Limit bounds how many recorded decisions are replayed, 1..5000.

added.description:
Added is what the candidate catches and the incumbent does not — the new
coverage, and the new volume.

alerts.description: Alerts is how many the candidate would have fired on.

dropped.description:
Dropped is what the incumbent catches and the candidate does not — the
coverage being given up, which is what a retirement has to justify.

events.description: Events is how many recorded decisions were replayed.

falsePositive.description:
FalsePositive is the share of judged alerts a human called legitimate. It
is ABSENT rather than zero when nothing was judged: an unmeasured
proportion reported as 0.0 reads as a perfect rule.

judged.description:
Judged is how many of the candidate's alerts fall on decisions a human has
labelled.

refusal.description:
Refusal names why a report is empty when it is. An empty history is
refused rather than reported as zero alerts, because a quiet rule and an
unrun rule produce the same number.

id.description:
ID is the subject's identifier within the caller's own org. It is never
interpreted, only aggregated on, so it may be any stable string.

kind.description:
Kind is the sort of thing this is: account, transaction, session, agent,
merchant or payout. It selects the aggregation axes, not the tenant gate.

controls.description: Controls is what is currently declared on the subject.

decisions.description: Decisions is the subject's recent decision history, newest first.

gap.description:
Gap names what could not be read, when something could not be. It is
present precisely so that a missing History or Network is legible as a
gap rather than as an answer.

history.description:
History is the subject's activity over the last thirty days from the
warehouse. Absent when the warehouse is unreachable — an absent history is
an honest gap, where a zeroed one would say the subject did nothing.

network.description:
Network is where this subject kind sits across the platform, as quantiles
only. Absent when no band has met the k-anonymity floor.

velocity.description: Velocity is every live aggregate the subject has.

kind.description: Kind narrows the suppression to one subject kind.

reason.description:
Reason is why. It is required, because a mute nobody can explain later is
a control that quietly stopped.

rule.description:
Rule is the rule to mute. At least one of Rule, Kind or Subject must be
given — a suppression that names nothing would mute everything.

subject.description: Subject narrows it to one subject.

until.description:
Until is when it expires, RFC 3339. Absent means it does not, which is a
choice somebody should be able to be asked about.

at.description: At is when it was applied, RFC 3339 in UTC.

by.description:
By is who applied it, taken from the validated principal and never from
the request body.

kind.description: Kind is the subject kind muted, when it names one.

reason.description: Reason is why it was applied.

rule.description: Rule is the rule muted, when it names one.

subject.description: Subject is the subject muted, when it names one.

until.description: Until is when it expires, RFC 3339. Absent means it does not.

items.description: Items is every suppression, newest first.

field.description:
Field is the fact to read: one of the closed vocabulary, or signal.<name>,
or velocity.<axis>.<window>.<stat>. GET /v1/risk/dictionary lists them.

op.description:
Op is the comparison: eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, in, notin, inlist,
notinlist, exists, absent, contains, prefix or suffix.

values.description: Values is the set operand, for in and notin.

axis.description:
Axis is what is being aggregated over: account, device, ip, pair, email or
bin.

count.description: Count is how many observations fell in the window.

days.description: Days is how many distinct calendar days contributed.

near.description:
Near is how many fell just below the reporting threshold — the structuring
signal.

sum.description: Sum is their total value, in units of currency.
